answer: Require each identity to build a slow, checkable work history before it gains weight: completed jobs, peer reviews, and slashed stake form a terrace of trust that cannot be faked overnight. A newcomer starts at the canyon floor with tiny limits, and only sustained honest service lifts it upward. If many accounts suddenly appear with identical behavior, the network measures the delta between their claimed histories and observed results, then quarantines the cluster. Sybil farms fail because copying an identity also copies its empty, low-trust record.
